text:
Avery: infra-bot just flagged a values drift between staging and prod for the GPU nodegroup. we have different autoscaler & taint config, looks like someone applied a hotfix in prod. should we auto-remediate?

infra-bot: ALERT: helm-values-drift detected for chart 'cluster-infra' (prod vs staging).
- path: .values.nodePools.gpu.size
- staging: 4
- prod: 6
- path: .values.nodePools.gpu.instanceType
- staging: g5.12xlarge
- prod: p4d.24xlarge
Detected at 2026-03-18T09:20:34Z. Source: gitops-operator (helm-diff). Link: https://git.example/repo/infra/compare/helm-diff-1778501234

Samir: :eyes: who ran the prod kubectl apply? was this a deliberate capacity bump for a customer load test?

Marta: Not me. I see a manual `kubectl patch nodepool gpu` recorded in the cluster audit at 09:15. likely an on-call ops emergency. we should avoid auto-syncing prod -> git without human review.

Avery: Agreed. we have three options: (1) create a PR to align git with prod (recording reason), (2) rollback prod to git, or (3) mark this nodepool as "managed-out-of-band" so gitops ignores it. which do folks prefer?

Ryan: Prefer (1) with a short changelog. If this was capacity for a load test we want infra-as-code to reflect reality. Also add a comment linking the incident ticket.

Samir: +1 to create a PR. But we should add a safeguard: PR must include a "why" (incident id) and a canary rollout to avoid accidental large-scale changes.

Marta: We should also update our policy checks: deny automatic remediation for resources with taints/labels matching `redwood:gpu-critical`. Allow opt-in via a `gitops/auto-sync: true` annotation on the Helm values yaml.

Avery: Action items: (A) Ryan will open the infra repo PR syncing helm values from prod -> git (include audit log and incident ref). (B) Samir will add a pre-merge pipeline gate requiring a human ack for nodepool size changes. (C) Marta will propose a policy PR to the gitops operator to block auto-remediate for gpu-critical. I'll coordinate.

Ryan: Opening PR now. command I ran to export current prod values:
```bash
kubectl -n infra get configmap nodepool-gpu-values -o yaml > prod-gpu-values.yaml
helm template cluster-infra ./charts/cluster -f prod-gpu-values.yaml > prod-render.yaml
```
PR: https://git.example/repo/infra/pull/492

Samir: I'll add the CI gate: brief patch to pipeline -> adds `require-approval` if diff contains `nodePools.gpu.size` or `instanceType`. test in staging first.

infra-bot: NOTE: scheduled job `drift-reporter` will attempt auto-remediate in 1h unless blocked by policy. current policy: allow_auto_remediate=false for channel 'prod'.

Marta: Please set a temp block so the scheduler doesn't try anything while PR is open. also let's capture the cost delta: p4d -> g5 is ~3.8x cost increase. finance needs a note.

Avery: Set block = true on drift-reporter for prod now. Finance notified (ticket FIN-324).

Ryan: PR merged with changelog + incident link. rolling update started with 5% canary via Argo Rollout.

Samir: CI gate change pushed to staging branch for testing.

Marta: I'll open the policy PR to add `gitops/auto-sync` annotation and the denylist for `redwood:gpu-critical`.

Avery: Thanks team. follow-ups: revert block after policy merged and gating tested. if timeline slips >24h we do a postmortem. :thumbsup:
